title: Simple filter
sql:
SELECT cust_id, status, amount
FROM sales.orders
WHERE status = 'paid'

title: Inner join with two predicates
sql:
SELECT c.region, SUM(o.amount) AS total
FROM sales.orders o
JOIN sales.customers c ON c.id = o.cust_id AND c.active = TRUE
WHERE o.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY c.region

title: Three filter kinds in one WHERE
sql:
SELECT id, cust_id, amount, region
FROM sales.orders
WHERE status = 'paid'
  AND amount BETWEEN 100 AND 500
  AND region IN ('EU', 'US')

title: Left join used as an anti join
sql:
SELECT c.id, c.email
FROM sales.customers c
LEFT JOIN sales.orders o ON o.cust_id = c.id
WHERE o.id IS NULL

title: Three way join
sql:
SELECT o.id, c.email, p.method, p.amount
FROM sales.orders o
JOIN sales.customers c ON c.id = o.cust_id
JOIN sales.payments p ON p.order_id = o.id AND p.amount > 0
WHERE c.region IN ('EU', 'US')

title: Self join for the previous order
sql:
SELECT curr.id, prev.id AS previous_id
FROM sales.orders curr
LEFT JOIN sales.orders prev
  ON prev.cust_id = curr.cust_id AND prev.created_at < curr.created_at
WHERE curr.status = 'open'

title: Correlated EXISTS
sql:
SELECT c.id, c.email
FROM sales.customers c
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM sales.orders o
  WHERE o.cust_id = c.id AND o.status = 'paid'
)

title: Correlated NOT EXISTS
sql:
SELECT c.id
FROM sales.customers c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM sales.orders o
  WHERE o.cust_id = c.id AND o.amount > 500
)

title: Scalar subquery in the projection
sql:
SELECT o.id, o.amount,
  (SELECT MAX(p.amount) FROM sales.payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id) AS largest_payment
FROM sales.orders o
WHERE o.amount > 50

title: IN against a subquery
sql:
SELECT c.id
FROM sales.customers c
WHERE c.region IN (
  SELECT r.code FROM sales.regions r WHERE r.active
)

title: Derived table with a filter
sql:
SELECT t.cust_id, t.total
FROM (
  SELECT o.cust_id, SUM(o.amount) AS total
  FROM sales.orders o
  GROUP BY o.cust_id
) t
WHERE t.total > 1000

title: CTE feeding a join
sql:
WITH paid AS (
  SELECT o.cust_id, SUM(o.amount) AS total
  FROM sales.orders o
  WHERE o.status = 'paid'
  GROUP BY o.cust_id
)
SELECT c.region, COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM paid p
JOIN sales.customers c ON c.id = p.cust_id
GROUP BY c.region

title: Two CTEs, one joined to the other
sql:
WITH paid AS (
  SELECT cust_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM sales.orders
  WHERE status = 'paid' GROUP BY cust_id
),
big AS (
  SELECT cust_id FROM paid WHERE total > 1000
)
SELECT c.id, c.email
FROM sales.customers c
JOIN big b ON b.cust_id = c.id
WHERE c.active

title: Recursive CTE over an org tree
sql:
WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (
  SELECT id, manager_id, 1 AS depth
  FROM hr.employees
  WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, e.manager_id, t.depth + 1
  FROM hr.employees e
  JOIN tree t ON e.manager_id = t.id
)
SELECT id, depth FROM tree WHERE depth < 5

title: Window function with QUALIFY-free ranking
sql:
SELECT id, cust_id, amount
FROM (
  SELECT id, cust_id, amount,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cust_id ORDER BY amount DESC) AS rn
  FROM sales.orders
) ranked
WHERE rn = 1

title: UNION of two branches
sql:
SELECT cust_id FROM sales.orders WHERE status = 'paid'
UNION
SELECT cust_id FROM sales.refunds WHERE settled

title: BETWEEN, LIKE, and a parameter
sql:
SELECT id, amount
FROM sales.orders
WHERE amount BETWEEN 10 AND 500
  AND email LIKE '%@example.com'
  AND status = $1

title: DISTINCT ON keeps the first row
sql:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (cust_id) cust_id, id, created_at
FROM sales.orders
ORDER BY cust_id, created_at DESC

title: LATERAL join to a top-three subquery
sql:
SELECT c.id, top.id AS order_id, top.amount
FROM sales.customers c
JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT o.id, o.amount FROM sales.orders o
  WHERE o.cust_id = c.id
  ORDER BY o.amount DESC
  LIMIT 3
) top ON TRUE
WHERE c.region = 'EU'

title: Simple filter
sql:
SELECT cust_id, status, amount
FROM sales.orders
WHERE status = 'paid'

title: QUALIFY on a window function
sql:
SELECT city, car_model, quantity
FROM dealer
QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY car_model ORDER BY quantity) = 1

title: QUALIFY references an output alias
sql:
SELECT city, car_model,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY car_model ORDER BY quantity) AS rank
FROM dealer
QUALIFY rank = 1

title: SEMI join
sql:
SELECT o.id, o.amount
FROM sales.orders o
LEFT SEMI JOIN sales.customers c ON c.id = o.cust_id
WHERE o.status = 'paid'

title: ANTI join
sql:
SELECT c.id
FROM sales.customers c
LEFT ANTI JOIN sales.orders o ON o.cust_id = c.id

title: CTE with a QUALIFY step
sql:
WITH recent AS (
  SELECT cust_id, id, amount, created_at
  FROM sales.orders
  WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT cust_id, id, amount
FROM recent
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cust_id ORDER BY created_at DESC) = 1

title: Recursive CTE with MAX RECURSION
sql:
WITH RECURSIVE t(n) AS (
  SELECT 1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT n + 1 FROM t WHERE n < 5
)
MAX RECURSION LEVEL 10
SELECT * FROM t

title: Named parameter marker
sql:
SELECT trip_distance, fare_amount
FROM samples.nyctaxi.trips
WHERE fare_amount < :fare_parameter

title: Three positional markers
sql: SELECT current_timestamp() + ?, ? * ? AS square

title: Join to a grouped subquery
sql:
SELECT c.id, t.total
FROM sales.customers c
JOIN (
  SELECT cust_id, SUM(amount) AS total
  FROM sales.orders
  GROUP BY cust_id
) t ON t.cust_id = c.id
WHERE t.total > 100

title: Correlated EXISTS
sql:
SELECT c.id
FROM sales.customers c
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM sales.orders o WHERE o.cust_id = c.id
)

title: Three CTE layers
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT cust_id, amount, status FROM sales.orders
),
paid AS (
  SELECT cust_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM base WHERE status = 'paid' GROUP BY cust_id
),
top AS (
  SELECT cust_id, total FROM paid WHERE total > 500
)
SELECT c.id, top.total
FROM sales.customers c
JOIN top ON top.cust_id = c.id

title: Limit the newest rows
sql:
SELECT id, created_at
FROM sales.orders
WHERE status = 'open'
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 25

title: Range and row limit
sql:
SELECT id, amount
FROM sales.orders
WHERE amount BETWEEN 10 AND 250
  AND status = 'paid'
LIMIT 10
